stories.title: California Governor Commutes Death Sentences for All Inmates on Death Row
stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced the commutation of death sentences for all 548 inmates on death row, converting their sentences to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. This decision reflects his stance against capital punishment, which he deems morally objectionable. Although California has not executed anyone in 20 years, this move does not abolish the death penalty or prevent future prosecutions from seeking it.
stories.event_title: California Governor Commutes Death Sentences for All Inmates on Death Row

story_report.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom said Nov. 5 that he would commute the death sentences of all 548 people on the state’s death row, changing their punishments to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The action affects current death sentences and does not itself authorize any prisoner’s release. California has not carried out an execution in 20 years, but the commutations do not by themselves abolish capital punishment under state law.

stories.title: Harmeet Dhillon Resigns as Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division
stories.summary: Harmeet Dhillon has resigned from her position as the assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice. Her resignation follows conflicts with DOJ leadership and comes shortly after the Republican Party's losses in the midterm elections. Dhillon had been in charge for approximately 18 months.
stories.event_title: Harmeet Dhillon Resigns as Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division

story_report.summary: Harmeet Dhillon resigned as assistant attorney general leading the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division after about 18 months, leaving its Senate-confirmed leadership post vacant. Her departure followed reported conflicts with DOJ leaders and occurred after Republican midterm losses, though available reporting does not establish a single cause. Dhillon said she had decided to leave weeks before the election, remained at the White House’s request and had not been asked to resign. Attorney General Todd Blanche said he accepted her resignation and praised her service.
